findings.description: A CSP limits where scripts and other content can load from, which reduces the impact of cross-site scripting.
findings.remediation: Define a Content-Security-Policy, starting with default-src 'self'.
findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy

findings.description: Browsers may guess a response's content type and run it as something dangerous (MIME sniffing).
findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options not set to nosniff

findings.description: The page can be embedded in a frame on another site, which enables clickjacking attacks.
findings.evidence: neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors present
findings.remediation: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY or a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none'.
findings.title: No clickjacking protection

findings.description: Cookies without HttpOnly can be read by JavaScript, so an injected script can steal them.
findings.remediation: Add HttpOnly to cookies that JavaScript does not need to read.
findings.title: Cookie missing HttpOnly flag

findings.description: Cookies without SameSite (or with SameSite=None but no Secure) are sent on cross-site requests, which enables CSRF.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict; SameSite=None requires the Secure attribute.
findings.title: Cookie missing or weak SameSite

findings.description: Response headers reveal exact software versions. This helps an attacker pick known exploits for that version.
findings.remediation: Remove version numbers from the Server and X-Powered-By headers.
findings.title: Server software and version disclosed

findings.description: Without a Referrer-Policy, browsers may send full URLs to other sites.
findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy

findings.description: A TCP port accepted a connection. Open ports are the attack surface of a host; each one should be there on purpose.
findings.evidence: port 8080 accepted a TCP connection; http (confirmed)
findings.remediation: Close or firewall ports that are not needed. Keep a list of expected open ports.
findings.title: Open TCP port
